mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has stabilized at +4.4% (t-0w) after declining from +7.0% (t-3w), signaling reduced lockdown intensity. This stabilization removes a suppressive force on retail-recreation demand, allowing RETAIL_REC to recover toward baseline over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from +7.0 to +4.4 over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days (-24.1%).

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has remained consistently negative and stable (range: -7.1 to -5.3%), indicating suppressed essential-goods shopping. This constraint on essential mobility reflects persistent behavioral caution that will continue to depress discretionary RETAIL_REC visits over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM range is -7.1 to -5.3 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week in either of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility spiked to +15.7% at t-1w then collapsed to +2.0% at t-0w, a 13.7-point drop. This volatility signals unstable outdoor-activity demand. If PARKS remains below +5% in the next week, outdoor substitution effects will not offset retail suppression, and RETAIL_REC will decline further.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below +5% in the current week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped 13.7 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS rebounds to above +10% and RETAIL_REC simultaneously increases by more than 3 percentage points in the same week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has remained severely depressed (range: -34.1 to -27.9%), indicating commuting collapse. When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both below -25%, retail-recreation demand is suppressed because foot traffic corridors are inactive. RETAIL_REC will remain below -20% over the next four weeks if both proxies stay in this regime.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -25% AND WORKPLACES below -25% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -27.9% and WORKPLACES at -25.0% at t-0w
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES rises above -20% while RETAIL_REC simultaneously increases above -15%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved from -33.9% (t-3w) to -25.0% (t-0w), a 8.9-point recovery over three weeks. This sustained workplace reopening trend signals policy relaxation. If this trend continues, RETAIL_REC will follow with a 4-week lag, rising above -20% by the end of the forecast period.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by more than 5 points over two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 8.9 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES declines by more than 3 points in the next week, or RETAIL_REC remains below -25% at the end of week 4.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown minimal week-on-week volatility (range: -28.0 to -23.1%), indicating a stable suppressed equilibrium. GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL are also stable. This behavioral lock-in suggests RETAIL_REC will persist near its current mean (-24.1%) over the next four weeks absent a shock to TRANSIT or WORKPLACES.
evidence_refs: fact:All three series show low volatility across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 8 percentage points from its current mean over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility exhibits high volatility (+8.3%, -4.7%, +15.7%, +2.0%), suggesting seasonal or weather-driven fluctuations. When PARKS is above +10%, substitution away from indoor retail occurs. Over the next four weeks, if PARKS volatility persists without sustained elevation, RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed as consumers lack consistent outdoor alternatives.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mean over any two-week window falls below +5%
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS standard deviation across four weeks is 9.2 percentage points
failure_condition: PARKS sustains above +12% for two consecutive weeks and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -15%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and RETAIL_REC are mechanically coupled: retail footfall depends on transit access. TRANSIT has improved from -34.1% (t-3w) to -27.9% (t-0w). If TRANSIT continues improving at this rate (1.5-2 points per week), RETAIL_REC will begin recovery in week 2 of the forecast, reaching -20% or higher by week 4.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by at least 1.5 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 6.2 points over three weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT declines or stagnates for two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC remains below -22% at the end of week 4.
